name: quantumnquandary
summary: a C# console duel about charging, defending, and reading your opponent. six actions, single-player and local two-player modes, and hand-built ASCII battle animations. the browser recreation reuses the original artwork.
problem: Expand rock-paper-scissors into a duel where resource management matters: save charges, predict an attack, or spend them on a decisive counter.
highlights: Six competing actions: Charge and Surrender cost nothing. Gun costs two, Mirror three, Kamehameha five, and Nuclear Bomb eight. Both players lock in before the round is revealed.
Solo or same-device duels: Play against a computer choosing from its affordable actions, or challenge a second player on one keyboard. Touch buttons provide the same actions.
Original ASCII animation: The title artwork, battle frames, and team credits come directly from the original C# source. The browser edition animates those frames in a fixed console-style playfield.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Choose single player or player vs player.
- Start with two charges and lock in an affordable action.
- Watch both moves resolve through the original ASCII frames.
- Continue until one action wins, then replay or return to the menu.

sections.heading: Under the hood & original credits
sections.body: Originally a C# console project, Final-Project-ITEC-102 (2023). Quert Alfonso M. Villafuerte is credited for player-vs-player, game mechanics, front-end game creation, and animation; Riz Ivan G. Verana for menus; Angelo S. Averion for single-player and menu design. The browser port separates the action rules, state machine, and extracted artwork.

sections.heading: Scope & browser adaptations
sections.body: A browser recreation using the original visual assets and documented rules, with valid charge deductions and consistent counters. It includes same-device multiplayer, not online matchmaking. The GitHub button links to this public browser edition; original team credits remain in-game. Browser fonts and timing may differ from the Windows console.
